html:
The Australian frontier wars were the conflicts between Aboriginal peoples and British settlers, from the arrival of the First Fleet in 1788 to the 1930s. Fighting moved across the continent as settlers took land for sheep and cattle.

Aboriginal groups fought back with raids and guerrilla war, led by men such as Pemulwuy near Sydney. Settlers, police and native police carried out massacres, such as at Myall Creek in 1838, after which seven settlers were hanged.

Tens of thousands of Aboriginal people died from violence, and many more from disease. The wars were long left out of national history. See Aboriginal Australians, Truganini and Stolen Generations.
